name: CSP Inspector
description: Parse Content-Security-Policy headers offline, explain directive fallbacks and source matching, and judge every resource as allowed, blocked or undetermined
help: One policy per line (a single header value); prefix a line with report-only: for Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, which reports but never blocks.
Set the document URL so 'self' can be resolved; list resources with their type and URL, or fill nonce/hash only for inline resources.

Matching covers 'self', 'none', nonce/hash, scheme sources (e.g. data:), host sources (port, wildcard subdomains, path prefixes) and default-src fallbacks; an omitted port matches only the default port.

Semantics that depend on the execution chain (strict-dynamic) answer "undetermined" instead of a fake allow. Duplicate directives keep the first one per spec; unknown directives only get a note. Resource URLs are never fetched and no reports are collected.

input.inline: Inline resources: fill nonce/hash and leave the URL empty
input.empty: Fill in a policy and press "Inspect"

errors.csp.too_large: Policy text exceeds the {{kb}} KB limit
errors.csp.no_result: No inspection result yet — run one first
errors.csp.unknown_directive: Unknown directive {{name}} (kept; may be a newer directive)
errors.csp.duplicate_directive: Directive {{name}} is duplicated; the first one wins per spec
errors.csp.strict_dynamic: script-src contains 'strict-dynamic': host sources are ignored for scripts and the outcome depends on the execution chain, so it is marked undetermined
errors.csp.unsafe_inline_ignored: {{name}} has both 'unsafe-inline' and a nonce/hash; browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline'
errors.csp.report_only_would_block: Report-Only policy {{index}} would block this resource (report only)
errors.csp.self_without_document: The policy uses 'self'; set the document URL to resolve it
errors.csp.unknown_type: Unknown resource type {{type}}, treated as unrestricted
errors.csp.undetermined: Some parts depend on the execution chain or are missing information, so they cannot be resolved statically
